summary: Weekly POC check-in to review latency heatmap from last week's runs, agree on model pinning for pilot traffic, discuss safe rollback/soft-failover options and next safety stops for private deployment. Focus on p50/p95 regressions across length buckets and how KV cache/quantization choices affected tail latency.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-19 14:30 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Ellen (NovaData ML Eng), Raj (Infra), Sofia (Product)
Links mentioned: latency heatmap (link), runbook draft (link), security FAQ (link)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for coming, we'll keep this to 45 minutes. Quick agenda — i sent a small heatmap and a couple of notes earlier, we'll walk through results, discuss which model version to pin for the pilot, and map out rollback / degraded paths.

[00:18] Ellen: yep thanks, i'm mostly interested in the tail, p95 spikes we saw yesterday — it looked like longer contexts went bad when we tried the new quantized variant.

[00:33] Carlos: right, quick context — we ran three variants: baseline v1.2 (float), v1.3-q8 (quantized), and v1.3-int4-lite. Each run had the same traffic mix you gave us: 70% short prompts (<=128 tokens), 25% medium (129-512), 5% long (>512). We also toggled prefix caching on/off for a subset.

[01:02] Raj: small note — our infra test had a slightly higher concurrency burst around 11:20am which may have skewed p95 on one of the runs. We throttled after but log shows the burst.

[01:18] Carlos: good call. The heatmap we shared highlights p50/p95 across length buckets and concurrency slices. Key takeaway: v1.3-q8 reduces median latency for short and medium by ~12-18% but has 40-65ms extra tail for long context when prefix cache misses and KV cache is cold. There's a transcription-ish issue in the logs where KV cache shows up as 'KV cash' in some rows, heads up.

[01:45] Ellen: that matches what we saw. For our UI use-case, p95 for long contexts is critical — long multi-turn threads are user visible. If quantization gives median wins but tail regressions, customers will notice.

[02:05] Maya: totally — that's the tradeoff. Our recommendation for the pilot is to pin traffic to v1.3-q8 for short + medium routes, and set a soft-fallback for long-context routes to v1.2 float. That avoids long-tail p95 regressions for long conversations while giving you cost savings on the bulk of traffic.

[02:28] Sofia: how would that routing work? Is that by route config in the Console?

[02:35] Carlos: yep — you can define per-route model selectors or use a rule: if prompt_length > 512 then use model v1.2, else v1.3-q8. We can also add a gradual rollout: start 80% short/medium on q8, shadow v1.2 for 20% to capture diffs.

[02:58] Ellen: shadowing sounds good; but what about rollbacks if we see hallucination or quality regress?

[03:10] Maya: we recommend two safeties: automated rollback by quality metric (your eval hooks), and manual canary failover. For the automated, you'd push evals that check for API-level quality regressions (we have an eval harness) — if a scoring threshold is crossed, Redwood can flip traffic back to the pinned stable variant. We also discussed keeping a "degraded mode" route where we reduce max tokens and increase truncation to lower tail latency while you investigate.

[03:42] Raj: want to double-check what metrics you need on our side to enable auto rollback?

[03:50] Carlos: primarily: rolling accuracy/regression score from your prompt set, delta in p95 latency and error rate. Format: CSV with timestamp, route, p50, p95, err_rate, quality_score. We can attach thresholds in the Console.

[04:12] Ellen: okay we'll produce that. One other thing — memory/kv cache warmup: the long-context p95 spike looked correlated with cold-starts after model switching. Any ways to mitigate?

[04:25] Carlos: yes — you can enable prefix caching and increase cache TTLs for routes expected to have repeated contexts, and use continuous batching to keep GPUs warm. For Private deployments we can set pre-warm schedules so that model variants stay resident. Note: more resident models means higher cost.

[04:48] Maya: we put some numbers in the heatmap — v1.3-q8 short/medium p50 42ms -> 35ms, p95 85ms -> 67ms. For long contexts p50 moves 220ms -> 190ms but p95 goes from 420ms -> 480-500ms on cold cache. The quantized-run showed occasional kernel-selection fallbacks which added jitter.

[05:15] Ellen: hmm those kernel fallbacks — are they deterministic? Could you pin stable kernels?

[05:22] Carlos: the runtime picks kernels based on sequence length and hardware; you can influence by forcing a compile profile or by pinning to a known-good execution path. For the pilot we can compile a profile that biases away from rare kernels; it's in the compilation panel. It will take one test run to validate.

[05:40] Raj: what's the cost delta we should expect if we keep two variants resident (v1.2 float + v1.3-q8) versus single-variant q8-only?

[05:50] Maya: rough sketch — single q8-only might be ~30-35% lower token-cost compared to float, but having both resident means reserved GPU memory and utilization inefficiencies, estimate a 10-12% overhead on top of q8-only. We put a cost-per-1M-token simulation in the sheet.

[06:12] Sofia: given our SLOs around 200ms p95 for UI, it sounds like we can't safely go q8-only until we tame the long-context tail. So pinned hybrid route is the plan?

[06:25] Ellen: agreed. We also need clarity on observability — token-level cost breakdowns and tracing for specific requests that hit fallback.

[06:33] Carlos: Console provides token-level cost and trace ids, and we add a route-level tracing hook you can attach to your logging pipeline. We'll share an example trace that maps tokens -> kernels -> latency contributions.

[06:52] Maya: quick aside on security: for Private / VPC pilots, we know NovaData asked about KMS integration and SOC2 logs. Raj, are you comfortable with the audit log cadence we showed?

[07:04] Raj: yes mostly; one ask — we need SAML SSO examples and an outline of how key rotation is handled for KMS. Is key rotation automatic?

[07:14] Carlos: rotation can be managed either by Redwood KMS orchestration or delegated to your customer KMS via HSM integration. We'll send the SAML wiring guide and KMS rotation patterns in the security FAQ.

[07:28] Maya: noted in next steps. back to model pinning specifics — so proposal: pin v1.3-q8 for 'chat-short' and 'chat-medium' routes, pin v1.2 for 'chat-long', shadow v1.2 on 15% of short+medium to keep a safety signal, and set an automated p95 threshold rollback at delta > 20% and quality delta > -0.05. Thoughts?

[08:00] Ellen: sounds reasonable. Can you lower the shadow to 10%? We want more exposure to q8 initially.

[08:06] Maya: we can do 10% shadow. We'll also add a soft-failover where if p95 crosses 250ms for 'chat-long' we switch to a degraded mode — reduce max_tokens from 1024 to 512 for a short window.

[08:20] Sofia: how are we alerted? Pager? Console?

[08:23] Carlos: alerts can be wired into your PagerDuty or Slack. We'll set up an alert template that triggers at set thresholds and includes trace ids + recent eval diffs.

[08:36] Raj: i want to circle back to one technical deep-dive point — the kernel selection failure you mentioned. Is that a runtime bug or expected behavior with quantized models on our GPU type?

[08:45] Carlos: expected behavior sometimes — certain attention kernels are more stable in float; q8 paths can hit an off-optimized kernel for long sequences. We saw that on the a100-driver mismatch we used in the test — there was a fallback to a generic kernel which increased latency. The fix options are: align driver/kernel versions, or pin a compiled kernel set as I mentioned.

[09:10] Ellen: driver alignment is likely easier for us. We'll try matching your recommended driver.

[09:18] Maya: ok noted as an action.

[09:23] (brief cross talk about next week's schedule)

[09:36] Carlos: quick demo — i won't share screen here but the heatmap link shows p95 across x-axis concurrency slices and y-axis length buckets. There's also a small 'stability' band that flags runs with >10% jitter. In your run, the stability band is orange for the long bucket with q8.

[09:58] Sofia: and what about rollback timing — if the automated rollback flips, how long to revert?

[10:05] Carlos: automated rollback is near-instant for routing in the control plane (~10-30s to complete global switch depending on route complexity). Model spin-up is the potential delay if the target variant isn't warm — that's where pre-warms matter.

[10:22] Ellen: okay we need pre-warm schedules for the long variant. Can Redwood keep v1.2 resident for weekends? We have low usage but don't want cold start Monday mornings.

[10:32] Maya: yes we can configure longer residency for v1.2, though we'll note cost implications. We'll add a weekend keep-alive schedule as a config snippet.

[10:44] Raj: one last security nit — does the audit trail include model version that served each request and the kernels used? We need that for compliance.

[10:53] Carlos: yes audit logs include model_id, model_version, and runtime evidence including kernel id and trace id. We'll include a sample log line in the security doc.

[11:06] Ellen: great. a couple of smaller items — we saw in the qualitative eval that v1.3-q8 introduced slightly different tokenization behavior for emojis and unicode — not sure if that's a tokenization drift or a decode artifact.

[11:20] Carlos: that's likely decode/bytepair nuance after quantization; we can run a tokenization diff. We'll add that to the shadow checks.

[11:29] Maya: To recap next immediate actions: Carlos will export the annotated heatmap and attach the compiled runbook by Friday 8/22; Ellen will run the 2x concurrency test and share logs by 8/26; Maya will send the security FAQ and SAML wiring by 8/21. We'll set the pilot routing: v1.3-q8 for short+medium, v1.2 float for long, 10% shadow of v1.2 on short+medium.

[11:58] Sofia: thanks — please label the runbook sections clearly so our infra team can follow.

[12:04] Maya: will do. Anything else?

[12:09] Raj: just schedule the security review meeting, prefer 8/28 morning.

[12:14] Maya: ok i'll propose times. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links and the CSV.

[12:20] (meeting ends)
